claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is in a solidified solid-solution state.
The temperature- and strain-rate-dependent dynamic behavior of Co-free FeNiCrMn can be explained by dislocation-mediated plasticity.
Interactions between dislocations and solute atoms influence the alloy's strength.
Interactions between dislocations and solute atoms influence the alloy's ductility.
Dislocation density and solute-atom distribution are the relevant structural mediators.
In situ high-energy X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy will be used to characterize the alloy.
The proposed regime spans room temperature to 800°C.
The proposed regime spans strain rates from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
At room temperature and 10^-3 s^-1, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have 20% higher yield strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At room temperature and 10^-3 s^-1, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have 15% higher ductility than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Specific processing conditions may alter dislocation density and solute-atom distribution.
Processing-dependent variation in dislocation density and solute-atom distribution may affect the predicted mechanical outcome.
The hypothesis is falsified if yield strength and ductility fail to increase by at least 15% and 10%, respectively, relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi at room temperature and 10^-3 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies 20% higher yield strength and 15% higher ductility, whereas falsification requires only 15% and 10% increases. Results below the stated prediction but above the lower falsification thresholds would neither satisfy the prediction nor falsify the hypothesis.
